To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
agents trained in referential games can learn to use compositional language, and that this ability is enhanced when the environment is structured and the input is symbolic.
(1) agents are able to learn to play referential communication games from pixel input and (2) the structure of the input data affects how communication emerges.
agents trained on referential games using raw pixel input can learn to communicate effectively and can do so by using a structured compositional language.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how communication can arise in an environment in which the agents do not have a priori knowledge of the world or of the language that will emerge.
the question of how agents can learn to communicate with each other, and what the properties of the resulting communication protocols are.
the question of whether and how communication protocols can emerge in the context of a reinforcement learning agent interacting with a complex environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the emergence of language from communication is possible in a reinforcement learning setting, and the degree of language structure depends on the degree of structure present in the input data.

the emergence of compositional communication protocols in the form of structured languages is more likely when the world is perceived as structured, and that the emergence of structured communication is most likely when the world has a structured compositional structure.
the degree of the structure found in the training environment affects the nature of evolved protocols.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the agents trained with symbolic input learn to communicate more efficiently and more reliably than those trained with pixel data.

(i) the evolved protocols are not always optimal, (ii) the evolved protocols do not always reflect the structure of the input, and (iii) agents trained on structured input are more likely to develop structured communication protocols.
we have shown how deep learning can be used to train agents to solve emergent communication tasks, and how this can help to understand the emergence of language.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the emergence of compositional communication protocols is possible in a reinforcement learning setting, and that this is possible even with raw pixels as input.
the emergence of compositional language is not a rare occurrence, but rather a natural consequence of the interaction between agents that need to coordinate in order to achieve a shared goal.
, by using contemporary machine learning methods, we can now study the emergence of compositional communication protocols at an unprecedented scale, and in a more realistic setting.
